what_its_for: Capivasertib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of breast cancer that is HR-positive (hormone receptor-positive) and HER2-negative. It is used together with another medicine called fulvestrant in adults whose cancer has spread to other parts of the body (advanced or metastatic breast cancer) and whose cancer has certain gene changes (PIK3CA, AKT1, or PTEN alterations). Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Take capivasertib by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember. This medicine is taken on a schedule: 4 days ON (Tuesday through Friday, for example), followed by 3 days OFF (Saturday through Monday). You will repeat this cycle every week. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific schedule.
dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) taken TWICE a day, for 4 days in a row, then 3 days off — every week. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but ONLY if it is within 8 hours of when you were supposed to take it. If more than 8 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store capivasertib at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture, heat, and light. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine past the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit while taking this medicine — they can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including vitamins, supplements, and herbal products. Some medicines (like certain antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines, and St. John's Wort) can interfere with how capivasertib works. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 weeks after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical help if you experience: severe diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting that is hard to control; a rash, skin peeling, sores in your mouth or on your skin (possible signs of a serious skin reaction); high blood sugar symptoms such as increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, or feeling very tired; signs of serious infection such as fever or chills; unusual tiredness or shortness of breath; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Capivasertib begins working in your body right away, but it may take several weeks to months before you or your doctor can see whether the cancer is responding. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well. Your doctor will check your progress with regular tests and imaging.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant — it may harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease — your dose may need to be adjusted or your doctor may monitor you more closely. Older adults: This medicine can be used in older adults, but side effects should be watched carefully.
